items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Clark Terry told me you can play higher than Cat Anderson

ctx.x: Well it’s another kind of education for sure, to go on the road with Clark Terry.

Absolutely. And to hear him play every night, a great experience. And then after that I came back to school and had more learning experiences, and getting ready to graduate I called up Clark and said, “Man, it’s like my last semester of school and I have no idea what I’m going to do.” And that’s then another reason I made this vow to myself is if I can help some kids not freak out, some young college students not freak out when it becomes their senior year, if I — and what I think all universities should do — can…

thinking about hiring me for this tour he has in Europe, but he said you told him I can play higher than Cat Anderson.” He said, “Man, I tried to get the cat to hire you, now when you go and take a solo, just play some high notes and he’ll like it.” So I said okay. So here I am this Eastman student, first of all you know when you’re in college there’s a lot of music you play in college that you never play anywhere else, because they don’t have the time to rehearse it, do you know what I’m saying? I don’t know if…
